repo.description:
### Impact
MariaDB rpm packages created a dedicated `mysql` user to run `mariadbd` as, and this user had its home dir set to the datadir. Such a configuration allowed a malicious user with `FILE` privilege to create various dot-files in `$HOME`. For example, a `.bash_profile` would be executed when someone does `su - mysql -s /bin/bash`.

MariaDB deb packages are not vulnerable, as the home there is set to `/nonexistent`.

### Patches
Fixed in 10.6.28, 10.11.19, 11.4.13, 11.8.9, 12.3.3, 13.0.2.

### Workarounds
Change the home for `mysql` user to something `mariadbd` cannot write to. For example `usermod -d / mysql` or `usermod -d /nonexistent mysql`.
